steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Line a baking sheet with foil.
Combine panko bread crumbs, parsley, dill, chives, extra-virgin olive oil, lemon zest, sea salt, and black pepper in a bowl. Taste and adjust with more salt if desired.
Rinse halibut fillets and pat dry with a paper towel.
Place halibut fillets onto the prepared baking sheet.
Generously spoon the herbed crumbs over the fish, and lightly press crumb mixture onto each fillet.
Bake in the preheated oven until crumb topping is lightly browned and fish flakes easily with a fork, 10 to 15 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Herb Crusted Halibut
raw_recipe.description: These halibut fillets are crusted with a variety of fresh herbs and panko bread crumbs to make a crispy, flavorful meal.
raw_recipe.name: Herb Crusted Halibut

review.reviewBody: I frequently prepare fish with this method – because I love it. And I frequently eat halibut, both out and preparing it myself – because I love it. (Get your fresh halibut now! The new season has just begun!) So I knew this recipe would be a sure thing, not likely to disappoint us. And it didn’t. It is a true gem and I know I will return to it often; not something I generally say about ANY recipe. After drying the filets I rubbed them lightly with olive oil, then salted and peppered them. I did not add salt to the topping, nor did I measure the olive oil, just added enough so the panko crumbs were lightly coated. Duncan, you have outdone yourself. This is a fresh tasting dish that allows the flavor of the beautiful halibut to shine. No heavy seasonings, no heavy, rich sauce. Excellent, especially served with a wild rice pilaf.

This was simple but delicious! I used tilapia instead of halibut but still turned out great. I didn’t have fresh dill so I used dried, but used fresh for the rest. I also added some olive oil and melted butter to the bread crumbs before I put on the fish so they adhered to the fish and stayed better. They also crisped up very nice with that addition. My 13 yo son rated it a 10, and coming from a fish lover, that is high praise!

I will definitely make this again! I did season the halibut first and i put a very small pat of butter on each filet...and i added about 1/2 cup of grated parmesan to the herb mixture! It was very good!

I added parmesan cheese to the herb mixture and more olive oil than it called for. I also smothered the halibut with olive oil first and a pat of butter then put the herb mixture on top. I also put the fillets in a shallow pan filled with wine at the bottom. It was amazing! Best halibut my family has had even in a restaurant. Will make again!

This was delicious af. I only had dry herbs - dill, herbes-de-Provence and thyme. I did add shredded parmesan (1/2+ cup), powdered garlic, plus double the amount of olive oil to the mixture. First coated the fillets with EVOO and a little Tumeric for the health benefits. Misread the instructions and baked for 30 minutes but it came out nicely browned and was quite delicious.

This was light and super moist--I think it's important to rub in some olive oil before the panko to keep it from drying out. I also broiled it for about 30 seconds right before serving for an extra cripsy topping. I just used dried herbs, whatever I had on hand, and eyeballed the measurements. It was delicious!

Substituted scallion for the chives, used meyer lemon olive oil and added a squirt from the lemon wedge that the rind came from. Dotted the fish with butter before topping with the bread crumbs. Delicious!

I love this recipe, I must have made it at least 5 times in the last month! The only change I made was to place the fish in a baking dish and then pour in enough white wine to cover the bottom of the pan. Very tasty!

I made this for our Easter dinner, and it was delicious! Make sure to season the fillets with salt and pepper before adding the herb/crumb topping. I served it with lemon wedges and a side of mayo, and everyone loved it. My fillets were pretty thick, so I ended up covering them with a piece of foil toward the end to avoid excessive browning on the panko crumbs. Definitely a keeper!
This recipe was both easy and delicious. I substituteed a lemon/citrus infused olive oil and cooked it on the gas grill. The panko topping was so flavorful. This will be new favorite at our house!

This is a great recipe! I followed the recipe pretty much to the letter except I seasoned the halibut with pink sea salt & fresh black pepper Before topping them with the panko mixture then after adding the panko mixture I drizzled olive oil over all of the fillets. The halibut was cooked perfectly! I love the fresh herbs especially the dill & lemon zest. In the future for a different flavors, I may add a thin coat of Dijon mustard before adding the panko mixture or squeeze fresh lemon juice over the halibut.
Very light and fresh. The different herbs were great compliment to the fish. I also added a small pat of butter. Definitely will make again.
soo delicious.. I used Macadamia nuts instead was an excellent swap

Absolutely delicious! Pay attention to how many fillets you are preparing. You may need to double the panko topping mixture. Each fillet should have a nice thick coat of the panko mixture on top. I have made this with fresh and frozen fish. Fresh is best, but defrost and bring fish to room temperature. I have used halibut and seabass.

I really piled the herb and panko topping on heavily, so I had to bake it a little longer than recommended, but it turned out delicious. It was not only the first time that I cooked halibut, but also the first time that I've eaten it. I will definitely be making this one again

I followed the recipe but used dried dill and parsley and green onions instead of chives because that’s what I had on hand. I had halibut steaks so I baked for 25 minutes. This has to be the best halibut I’ve ever had! Even my boyfriend told me I outdid myself. I’m going to make it again for my parents next month. I wish I could give 10+ stars! Thank you for sharing this delicious recipe, the flavor was perfect and not overpowering. Yummy!

This was so quick and easy to make and I loved the crunchiness. I didn't have fresh parsley so I had to use dry but other than that, I followed the recipe exactly as written and I don't think there's one thing that I'd change. The flavor/spices were on point and I will be making this again.
Delicious and so simple. Made it during lunch brake!
One change for added flavour....First coat the fillets in olive oil, and sprinkle liberally with Old Bay Seasoning; cover with cling film and place in the fridge overnight.
Delicious, flavorful and moist and so easy to make. Winner!
